channel.title: CorX Labs — releases and notes
channel.description: Model releases and technical write-ups from CorX Labs, an independent AI research lab in Jamaica.

item.title: Benchmark index: 12 new models, 201 in all
item.dc:creator: Nathan Lyttle
item.description: The benchmark index now holds 201 models from 42 labs. New: Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2, GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol, GPT-6.1 Terra, Gemini 4 Argon, Carbon, Hydrogen and Neon, Qwen4-Max, MiniMax-M3.1-Flash and ERNIE 5.5 Flash Preview. Most of these launches led on benchmarks the index does not track, so most new rows have specs and prices but few scores. GPT-6.2 Astra now has the highest published GPQA Diamond score in the index, 97.0%, from its system card. Claude Sonnet 5.5's cache-read price is corrected to $0.10 per million tokens. The index.

item.title: helix-lm 2.5: a benchmark for TriStream-2, and Pinxit, a painter
item.dc:creator: Nathan Lyttle
item.description: helix-lm 2.5.0 is on PyPI. 2.4 adds a benchmark for TriStream-2, the singing model: resynthesis, voice conversion, singing from written notes and pitch control, with 95% intervals, run after every training eval. So far it has scored only the baselines, on a CPU. 2.5 adds Pinxit, which paints a photo stroke by stroke and keeps the strokes, so a painting can be replayed, changed and undone. Neither model is trained yet: no GPU run has been made for Pinxit, and painting from words does not work well enough to use. The HELIX block itself is unchanged and still has no trained checkpoints. The HELIX page.

item.title: Pluvium 0.5.7: the fourth GPU run, and what stopped it
item.dc:creator: Nathan Lyttle
item.description: Pluvium 0.5.7 is on PyPI. The fourth GPU run of Pluvium-500 trained for 11.6 hours, to step 8,625, with a best held-out loss of 0.734. It was planned for 24 hours and a molab notebook shuts down after 12, so it stopped before it was scored, and the restarts failed on a device error. 0.5.6 ends a run on molab half an hour early with 1.5 hours kept for scoring and publishing, and fixes the device error. 0.5.7 scores each held-out forecast at 2,000 cells so scoring ends in time. Pluvium-500 has no scores yet; the results on the page still come from pluvium-small. The Pluvium page.

item.title: Automa 1.9.18: updates on a phone that is nearly full
item.dc:creator: Nathan Lyttle
item.description: Automa 1.9.18 is out. automa update now checks the storage before it starts, clears what is safe to clear (leftovers of an earlier update, unfinished downloads, Termux's package files, npm's download cache) and, when there is still too little room, says how much is free and how much it needs before anything changes. Running out of storage is no longer reported as a dropped connection, and an update tried several times keeps one copy of the database. Nothing else changes in the app. Download the APK (24.9 MB); it installs over 1.9.17 and keeps your data. Every release.

item.title: Automa 1.9.17: App Studio reads like a code editor, and App Inspector gets a chat
item.dc:creator: Nathan Lyttle
item.description: Automa 1.9.17 is out. App Studio reads like a code editor: open files are tabs, a line under the editor shows the line and column, the language and whether the file is saved, and on a phone a row of keys adds the symbols the keyboard hides. When a free model is busy or at its limit, the reply offers Try again and Ask another model; one tap switches to a model that is answering and sends your message again. App Inspector has a chat of its own, on the free models with no key or on Claude with your own key, and Decode again repairs a project opened before. 50 fixes, and IMY 1.1.2 in Terminals. Download the APK (24.9 MB); it installs over 1.9.16 and keeps your data. Every release.

item.title: Automa 1.9.16: IMY's console reads like the file you are writing
item.dc:creator: Nathan Lyttle
item.description: Automa 1.9.16 is out. IMY's console now reads like the file you are writing: one line names the program file your code becomes, each line stands behind its number, and the code it became appears under it with its own number. :run prints what your program prints and nothing else. Pasted lines are numbered one by one, :: end is code, and a result no longer lands in the line you are typing. Nothing else changes in the app. Open Terminals and tap IMY: the tile says Tap to update. Download the APK (25.3 MB); it installs over 1.9.15 and keeps your data. More about IMY: its section. Every release.

item.title: Automa 1.9.15: IMY comes to Terminals
item.dc:creator: Nathan Lyttle
item.description: Automa 1.9.15 is out. IMY comes to Terminals: write code your own way under a first line that says what you are building, and IMY checks it, turns it into another programming language as you type and runs it, without changing your file. A menu on the IMY tile picks the language: Python, JavaScript, Ruby, Rust, C, Go, Assembly and thirteen more. IMY knows 48 languages and builds and runs 42 of them when the language's own tool is installed. It works with Automa's free models with no key, or with your own Anthropic, OpenAI or Gemini key. A Check button asks every free model for one word and marks the ones closed at their provider, and there is one more free model, LFM3 1.7B. Download the APK (25.3 MB); it installs over 1.9.14 and keeps your data. Every release.

item.title: Automa 1.9.14: Automa in your language
item.dc:creator: Nathan Lyttle
item.description: Automa 1.9.14 is out, in your language. Account, Language offers Auto and 40 languages: Auto follows your phone or browser, and dates, numbers and times follow your language and country. The main screens are built in for every language, and the rest of the board is translated by Automa's free models and kept on your server; only Automa's own wording is sent, never your chats, tasks, names or files. Arabic, Persian, Hebrew and Urdu read right to left. Agents write to you in your language, and Moan keeps Patois for English. The connect screen and, on Android 13 and newer, the app's own notices follow the choice too. Download the APK (25.1 MB); it installs over 1.9.13 and keeps your data. Every release.

item.title: Automa 1.9.13: model lists that keep themselves current, and security fixes
item.dc:creator: Nathan Lyttle
item.description: Automa 1.9.13 is out. Model lists now keep themselves current: an agent's model choice, App Studio, the Terminals menus and the chat's Newest models follow a public catalog of the major makers' models, newest first, with Claude Fable 5.2, Gemini 4 Carbon and Hydrogen and Qwen 4 Max added. Three new free models: Ling 3.2 Flash, ERNIE 5.5 Flash Preview and Particle 1. The free models' key is stored scrambled, the phone's database password and app key are locked to Termux on every install, sign-in tries are counted per real caller, and other sites can no longer frame the board. On the phone, PostgreSQL 18 runs 4 helper processes instead of 7. Download the APK (23.9 MB); it installs over 1.9.12 and keeps your data. Every release.

item.title: Automa 1.9.12: safe start, troubleshooting and fewer stops on the phone
item.dc:creator: Nathan Lyttle
item.description: Automa 1.9.12 is out. When Termux closes with "[Process completed (signal 9)]", Android has ended its processes: Android 12 and newer do that once all apps together run more than 32 in the background, and every Android does it when memory runs low. The database on the phone now runs fewer processes and uses less memory, and the new automa keep-alive lifts Android's process limit over Wireless debugging and takes Termux off battery optimisation. After three stops in a row, Automa starts in safe mode, with agents, schedules and plugins off, and says why. automa troubleshoot checks and repairs what it safely can, and a Refresh button loads the board again. Download the APK (23.9 MB); it installs over 1.9.11 and keeps your data. Every release.

item.title: Pluvium-500: the first checkpoint is on Hugging Face
item.dc:creator: Nathan Lyttle
item.description: The first weights of Pluvium-500, the full-size rain network, are on Hugging Face: CorxLabs/Pluvium-500, folder checkpoint/stage_a/best. Stage A is the training on reanalysis. Every 30 minutes the trainer scores the network on 32 forecast times from the held-out year, and this folder keeps the weights with the lowest loss so far. It is not the finished model. Training on real GFS runs, calibration and the scores on a held-out year come after it, and the results on the Pluvium page still come from pluvium-small. The Pluvium page.

item.title: Scam Radar: check any link, a live feed and a map
item.dc:creator: Nathan Lyttle
item.description: Scam Radar now checks a link you paste into it. It judges the address in your browser with the scanner's own rules, looks up the scanner's record for the site, and, where the scan server is running, visits the page as plain text and reads its code. The page also has a feed of named scam sites going live and being taken down, the kinds of scam and the scam kits in use, and the batches of names registered by script. A second page draws the named sites on a globe, grouped into campaigns that show the same lure. In its first day the scanner visited 9,713 sites and found 1,894 live and high risk. It has recorded no takedowns yet, and found none aimed at Jamaica.

item.title: Automa 1.9.11: plain words when the connection drops
item.dc:creator: Nathan Lyttle
item.description: Automa 1.9.11 is out, with fixes from a scan of the whole app. Saving your name or photo, and the App Studio page an invited collaborator uses, say "Can't reach" in plain words instead of "Failed to fetch" when the connection drops. An agent's settings page loads its extra settings by itself once Automa answers again. After a reconnect, pages you had already left stop asking the server every 10 seconds. Download the APK (23.9 MB); it installs over 1.9.10 and keeps your data. Every release.

item.title: Pluvium 0.5.5: three GPU runs, none finished yet
item.dc:creator: Nathan Lyttle
item.description: Pluvium 0.5.5 is on PyPI. The forecast itself has not changed since 0.5.2. Versions 0.5.3 to 0.5.5 are about training Pluvium-500, the full-size network. Three GPU runs have been tried and none has finished: the first stopped after 138 minutes, the second right after it measured one forecast at 38.6 GB on the 96 GB card, and the third trained on that card for the first time, then stopped when a data file was missing. The fixes are in: a batch that cannot fit is not tried, a stopped run starts again and keeps its log, and every data file is checked before training starts. Pluvium-500 is not trained or published yet. The Pluvium page.

item.title: Scam Radar: live scam websites, by country
item.dc:creator: Nathan Lyttle
item.description: Scam Radar is live. A scanner watches more than 18 million domains and every new web certificate, visits the suspicious sites, and records when each scam site goes up and when it is taken down. The page shows the scams aimed at your own country first, a leaderboard of the most targeted countries and most faked brands, and the week's takedowns. It publishes new scans by itself, about once an hour. Sites are only named on strong evidence.

item.title: Pluvium 0.5: one command to a forecast, and when in the day it rains
item.dc:creator: Nathan Lyttle
item.description:
Pluvium 0.5.2 is on PyPI. pluvium now --country JM goes from nothing to a forecast: it sets the country up, downloads or trains a blend, reads the newest runs and prints the forecast, with no GPU. For the first three days each place now gets the six-hour period in which rain is most likely; on Jamaica's wet days that placed the rain 7.8% better than the usual pattern alone. Parishes get their own view.

The full-size network is still not trained: its GPU training only started working in 0.4.3, and the first run stopped after 138 minutes. The model page has the details.

item.title: Pluvium 0.3 — a full year in seven places, and hurricane tracks
item.dc:creator: Nathan Lyttle
item.description:
Pluvium 0.3.0 is out. Over a full year, April 2025 to March 2026, in seven places on four continents, Pluvium Blend had the best skill of every ECMWF and NOAA system for rain on days 1 to 7. Version 0.3 learns after every verified day, handles record storms, labels alerts in plain terms, and adds Pluvium Cyclone, hurricane tracks from the same six systems.

The losses are published too: it does not lead at 50 mm, it under-forecast Hurricane Melissa's rain over Jamaica, and its hurricane tracks trail the National Hurricane Center's official forecast. It is a research model, not an official forecast. The model page has the charts.

item.title: Pluvium — rain, hour by hour, for every Caribbean town
item.dc:creator: Nathan Lyttle
item.description:
Pluvium forecasts rain for every town and village in the Caribbean, hour by hour, three days ahead: the chance of rain each hour, whether it will be drizzle, showers or a thunderstorm, when it will start, how long it will last and how much will fall. It runs on the NatureV1 engine, and Pluvium Blend pools six operational forecast systems into daily rain chances out to 14 days.

Tested against ECMWF and NOAA on real archived forecasts for Jamaica, the small model had the highest skill of any single system for rain on days 1 and 2 in July and August 2025, and lost in May and June 2025, after a wet April it had never trained on. It is a research model, not an official forecast. The code is on PyPI as pluvium, under Apache 2.0. The model page has the results and the limits.

item.title: Automa 1.9.10: starting up and reconnecting
item.dc:creator: Nathan Lyttle
item.description: Automa 1.9.10 is out. While Automa is still starting on the phone, the connect screen shows which step it is on and how long it has waited. When the connection drops and comes back, the board reconnects by itself instead of showing "Failed to fetch", and a dropped connection no longer sends you to sign-in. Download the APK (23.9 MB); it installs over 1.9.9 and keeps your data. Every release.

item.title: Automa 1.9.9 — waits out the slow-down
item.dc:creator: Nathan Lyttle
item.description: Automa 1.9.9 is out, with fixes from a scan of every page and a live run of the app. When the free AI service asks Automa to slow down, Automa now waits the minute it asks for and carries on, instead of failing the reply. Home no longer shows cards for chats and tasks you deleted, and deleting a chat or task cancels the retries still waiting for it. Download the APK (23.9 MB); it installs over 1.9.8 and keeps your data. Every release.

item.title: Automa 1.9.8 — fixes under the hood
item.dc:creator: Nathan Lyttle
item.description: Automa 1.9.8 is out. Automa on the phone now starts even when an old queued run can’t be verified, cancelling a queued run no longer stalls the scheduler for 30 seconds, and web search falls back to Bing when DuckDuckGo refuses. Free-model agents hand a task back for your review after answering, and drop a tool that fails three times in a row. Download the APK (23.9 MB); it installs over 1.9.7 and keeps your data. Every release.

item.title: Meet Automa: An AI Agents App Made in Jamaica
item.dc:creator: Nathan Lyttle
item.description: Meet Automa 1.9.7, an Android app, made in Jamaica, that runs a whole company of AI agents from a phone: hire agents, chat with them, hand them tasks and approve what matters. It runs on twenty-plus free chat models and two free image models with no key, no account and no card — including Moan, a Jamaican model that answers in Patois and cites Jamaican news, law and government sources — or on your own Claude, GPT and Gemini keys. App Studio builds apps in 69 languages, and the server can run on the phone itself. Download the APK (22.9 MB); an APKPure listing is pending review. Every screen in the app.

item.title: Building a Hurricane AI in Jamaica on One GPU
item.dc:creator: Nathan Lyttle
item.description: NatureV1 is an open-source AI weather and hurricane model, built in Jamaica in about a week on a single GPU. How it was built — three design bets, a hosted notebook that wiped its disk every session, the number that showed the hurricane heads learned something — what it gets right on storms it never saw, and where a red team broke it.

item.title: NatureV1 released — trained, scored and red-teamed
item.dc:creator: Nathan Lyttle
item.description:
NatureV1's first full run is complete, and every result was measured on data it never trained on. On 59 storms from the held-out 2017, 2019 and 2021 Atlantic seasons its hurricane track beats a physics-only steering track and straight-line extrapolation at every lead — 163 km at 24 hours and 739 km at 72 — and on the unseen 2023 El Niño season it beat steering for every one of the seven hurricanes. Its full-atmosphere rollout has skill against persistence and climatology out to 72 hours.

It is a research model, not an operational forecast. Its track errors are 2.5 to 4.5 times the National Hurricane Center's, it underestimates strong storms, its rapid-intensification probabilities are far too high, and it missed Hurricane Otis's explosive intensification entirely. A red-team section on the model page lists where it breaks. Weights, results and evaluation scripts: Sigmandndnns/NatureV1-500.

item.title: NatureV1 — a weather and hurricane model, in training
item.dc:creator: Nathan Lyttle
item.description:
NatureV1 is an 89.18M-parameter probabilistic model of the atmosphere. It forecasts global weather out to five days and, for a tropical cyclone, its track as six weighted scenarios, its intensity, the chance of rapid intensification and the chance of landfall, every number with an uncertainty. It is built on iHELIX, an attention engine whose heads have physical radii in kilometres over the real sphere.

The first full training run is in progress and no forecast skill is claimed. Do not use it for real decisions; for a live storm, use the National Hurricane Center. Live checkpoints: Sigmandndnns/NatureV1-500. Code: naturev1 on PyPI, Apache 2.0.

item.title: Automa — run your AI company from your phone
item.dc:creator: Nathan Lyttle
item.description: Automa is an Android app for running a company of AI agents from a phone. The agents run on a server — the phone itself under Termux, or a machine over HTTPS — and Automa is the control surface: what needs you, tasks, routines, scoped connections, and a Device Files channel agents can request files through. There is no public download link yet.

item.title: HELIX — linear scaling with exact long-range recall
item.dc:creator: Nathan Lyttle
item.description: HELIX is a sequence architecture that scales linearly in context length while keeping exact long-range recall, by braiding a local window, a delta-rule recurrent state and a landmark-tree index over one residual stream. Published as helix-lm under Apache 2.0, with a tested reference implementation. There are no trained checkpoints.

item.title: CorX3.8-27B — Jamaica's first large open-weight LLM
item.dc:creator: Nathan Lyttle
item.description:
CorX3.8-27B is a 27-billion-parameter Jamaican Patois-speaking assistant, third in the CorX line after CorX1.5 and TriStream. It speaks Patois by default and switches to standard English on request, answers directly, holds boundaries, and carries everyday Jamaican cultural reference — while keeping the general reasoning, code and maths of its base model.

It is a fine-tune of the open-weight Qwen3.8-27B base (Apache 2.0), fully merged and standalone. It runs in 4-bit on a single ~24GB GPU. For factual questions, CorX Labs ships a retrieval layer that grounds answers on real Jamaican sources. Repository: Sigmandndnns/CorX3.8-27B.

item.title: TriStream-SVS — singing voice synthesis, factored by design
item.dc:creator: Nathan Lyttle
item.description:
TriStream-SVS is a 321.8M parameter singing voice synthesis model that builds the source-filter theory of human voice production into its architecture as a hard constraint: three parallel encoder streams for pitch, timbre and breath texture, combined only in a late fusion trunk. Zero-shot voice cloning via a contrastive speaker encoder, an adversarial singer head with gradient reversal as an anti-memorisation mechanism, and a rectified flow-matching decoder that generates in roughly 32 sampling steps.

Released. Repository: Sigmandndnns/TriStream-SVS-300M.

item.title: 3 Billion Tokens on One GPU: How CorX1.5 Was Trained
item.dc:creator: Nathan Lyttle
item.description: Everyone asks how 3 billion training tokens fit on a single GPU. They never had to. A technical breakdown of what actually has to fit in VRAM for a 158M-parameter model, the 6 GB memory-mapped token file the dataset really lives in, sequence packing, gradient accumulation, and why the whole pretraining run is only about 5,700 optimiser steps.

item.title: Announcement: CorX Labs releases CorX1.5
item.dc:creator: CorX Labs
item.description: CorX Labs, an independent AI research lab in Jamaica, has released CorX1.5 — a 158-million-parameter language model designed and trained entirely from scratch by a single developer on a single GPU, under the Apache 2.0 licence.

item.title: CorX1.5 — a 158M parameter language model built from scratch
item.dc:creator: Nathan Lyttle
item.description:
CorX1.5 is an open-source language model with roughly 158 million parameters, built entirely from scratch by a single developer in Jamaica. It is a custom decoder-only transformer using RoPE positional encoding, SwiGLU feed-forward layers and RMSNorm, with learned role embeddings, assistant-only loss masking, 10 layers, a 1,024-token context window and a 32,768-token custom BPE vocabulary.

Trained in three stages — pretraining on ~3B tokens across 25 open datasets, distillation from a larger teacher model, then reasoning training with step-by-step <think> blocks. Released under Apache 2.0 on Hugging Face.
